propositions: The completion verifier discovers file contents agentively via repeated tool calls (read_file/search_files), incurring 84-158 requests per run dominated by round-trip overhead rather than token cost; 67-82% of distinct file reads overlap with declared file_impact.

Prefetching bounded file_impact contents into the verifier context can reduce discovery overhead, but the prefetch set must respect the close gate's graph=False contract (own file_impact only, no subtree walk) while still supporting graph=True deep-review subtree union.

The assemble_context function is shared by the completion gate, dimension reviews, and workflows; prefetch must be opt-in via an explicit parameter (default None) so generic review callers produce byte-identical output.

Prefetched file bodies and skeleton-compressed stubs must be ranked, clamped to a 30k-token budget, included in physical_context_ceiling accounting, and labeled with a trusted anti-anchoring paragraph in the system prompt before the volatile marker so both primary and recovery successors inherit it.

Live A/B testing on two closed tickets demonstrates prefetch reduces baseline request count by 30-56% with equal verdict class (target >=20% met), achieving this by eliminating opening discovery excursions that the baseline otherwise performs.
